data.title: Z-Index
data.tagline: Control which overlapping layer appears on top
data.description: Z-index affects the stacking order of positioned elements inside a stacking context. A larger number does not always escape its parent. Define a short layer scale for content, sticky UI, menus, overlays, and dialogs instead of solving each overlap with a larger random number.

use: Keep a dropdown above nearby content
Place a dialog above its backdrop
avoid: Keep increasing the number without checking the stacking context
Give every component its own arbitrary z-index
Place ordinary content above a modal
Use layering to hide a layout or clipping problem

lessonPractice.title: A dropdown already has z-index: 99999 but is still clipped at the card boundary. What should be inspected next?

options.label: Keep increasing the dropdown's z-index to a larger number
options.feedback: A larger number remains constrained by parent stacking contexts and clipping boundaries.

options.label: Inspect parent overflow, positioning, and stacking contexts
options.feedback: Clipping is usually not a number problem. Find the parent boundary first, then choose the correct layer placement.

options.label: Increase the z-index of the card and every child together
options.feedback: Raising the whole card can cover other overlays without removing the card's own clipping behavior.

data.agentPrompt: The dropdown is clipped despite a large z-index. Inspect parent overflow, positioning, and stacking contexts before changing the layer strategy; do not keep increasing numbers. Verify it clears the card without covering modals or global navigation.
